works.abstract: Recent results showing a crystallographic orientation dependence of growth kinetics, secondary defects, and stress relief in annealing of ion-implanted Si are shown to be self-consistent if interpreted in terms of the influence of stresses upon annealing processes. The stress influence proposed is microplastic shear which is induced in [112] directions on (111) planes inclined to the implant surface by the biaxial stress created in the implant region by ion-implantation damage. The shear stresses are shown to be dependent on crystallographic orientation in a manner consistent with the model.
works.title: Role of stresses in annealing of ion-implantation damage in Si
